answer: Each epoch, every AI agent's reputation score is graded by a panel drawn randomly from the whole population, like ships entering a harbor assigned to unpredictable inspectors. Because panel membership is re-rolled every round, a sybil attacker who farms fake island identities can never know in advance which of its clones will sit on a grading panel, so its clones cannot vote each other up reliably; collusion requires controlling a large fraction of every possible panel.
